card.name: Linking words before drug-effect verbs
card.fires_on: Small linking words (to, that, of, may) right after a drug or drug class, just before a verb describing an effect such as prolong, affect, produce or exacerbate. Most often in QT-prolongation interaction statements.

modes.label: Drugs known to / that prolong
modes.description: "to" or "that" after "drugs known" or "drugs", before "prolong the QT interval".
modes.example: Concomitant use of BESPONSA with drugs known<< to>> prolong the QT interval or induce Tors

modes.label: Capable of / may before an effect
modes.description: "of", "to" or "may" after a named drug, before a verb for an adverse effect.
modes.example: All sulfonylurea drugs, including glipizide, are capable<< of>> producing severe hypoglycemia [

card.writes: Suggests the next word is an effect verb like prolong, affect or exacerbate, rather than the listed suppressed tokens.
card.plain: It marks the small word after a drug name that leads into what the drug may do, like "drugs that prolong QT".
